I. Construction
It is anticipated that this improvement will consist of five (5) contracts which are as follows:
   Reconstruction of the I.C.G. RR. Bridge over Lincoln Highway would include the reconstruction of Lincoln Highway from west of Indiana Street to west of Olympian Way. Drainage within this vicinity would also be included as part of this contract.
2. Main storm sewer from Chicago Road to west of Indiana Street.
3. Grading, paving and other appurtenances from Chicago Road to west of Indiana Street.
4. Main storm sewer from west of Olympian Way to Cicero Avenue.
5. Grading, paving and other appurtenances from Olympian Way to Cicero Avenue.
Prior to letting the bridge contract, the work for the Transportation Center would commence. The construction work elements will be scheduled so that traffic will be maintained throughout construction with at least one lane of traffic in each direction. Continuous access will be maintained to abutting properties. (See Appendix I, "Construction Procedures and Maintenance of Traffic, I.C.G. RR. Bridge over U.S. Route 30").
The project detour plan is designed to maintain traffic in each direction during the entire construction period. Temporary ingress and egress will be provided to business and commercial establishments in order to minimize the economic impact on services performed. Local access will be maintained even though through traffic may be detoured on some segments of the improvement. In all cases, the detour plan will be promulgated to minimize any probable safety hazard to the motoring public and residents of the area during construction.
The estimated cost of construction, right-of-way, and engineering for the project as proposed, is $13, 184,000.00.
J. Aesthetics
The Village of Park Forest has twenty-foot right-of-way along the south side of Lincoln Highway. Within this right-of-way were screen plantings eight feet or more in height. The proposed widening of Lincoln Highway would have resulted in the loss of these plantings unless they were relocated by the Fall of 1972 or the Spring of 1973.
